cudssHandle_t.doc:
The structure holds the cuDSS library context (device properties, system information, execution controls like `cudaStream_t`, etc.).

The handle must be initialized with [`cudssCreate()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudsscreate "cudssCreate") or [`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg") prior to calling any cuDSS API which takes it as an argument.
The handle must be destroyed to free up resources after using cuDSS with [`cudssDestroy()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdestroy "cudssDestroy").

cudssMatrix_t.doc:
The structure is a lightweight wrapper around standard dense/sparse matrix parameters and does not own any data arrays.
Matrix objects are used to pass matrix of the linear system, as well as solution and right-hand side (even if these are in fact vectors).
Currently, cuDSS matrix objects can have either one of the two underlying matrix formats: dense and 3-array CSR (sparse). Additionally,
they can represent non-uniform batches of matrices or distributed (in the MGMN mode).

Matrix objects should be created via [`cudssMatrixCreateDn()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssmatrixcreatedn "cudssMatrixCreateDn") (for dense matrices) or
[`cudssMatrixCreateBatchDn()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssmatrixcreatebatchdn "cudssMatrixCreateBatchDn") (for a batch of dense matrices) or
[`cudssMatrixCreateCsr()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssmatrixcreatecsr "cudssMatrixCreateCsr") (for sparse matrices in CSR format) or
[`cudssMatrixCreateBatchCsr()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssmatrixcreatebatchcsr "cudssMatrixCreateBatchCsr") (for a batch of sparse matrices in CSR format). After use, matrix objects should be destroyed
via [`cudssMatrixDestroy()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssmatrixdestroy "cudssMatrixDestroy"). For distributed matrices, one can additionally call [`cudssMatrixSetDistributionRow1d()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssmatrixsetdistributionrow1d "cudssMatrixSetDistributionRow1d") to define how the matrix is distributed.

Matrix objects can be modified after creation via [`cudssMatrixSetValues()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssmatrixsetvalues "cudssMatrixSetValues") and [`cudssMatrixSetCsrPointers()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssmatrixsetcsrpointers "cudssMatrixSetCsrPointers") (and similar APIs for batches).

Information can be retrieved from a matrix object by calling [`cudssMatrixGetFormat()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssmatrixgetformat "cudssMatrixGetFormat") followed by either [`cudssMatrixGetDn()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssmatrixgetdn "cudssMatrixGetDn") or [`cudssMatrixGetCsr()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssmatrixgetcsr "cudssMatrixGetCsr") depending on the format returned.

cudssData_t.doc:
The structure holds internal data (e.g., factors related data structures) as well as pointers to user-provided data.
A single object of this type should be associated with solving a specific linear system.
If multiple systems with the same datatype(!) are solved consecutively the object can be re-used (all necessary internal buffers will be re-created per necessity).

Note: by default, the library allocates device memory required for performing LU factorization and storing the LU factors internally. All data buffers of this kind are kept inside the data object.
To change this default behavior, one can set a [`cudssDeviceMemHandler_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdevicememhandler-t "cudssDeviceMemHandler_t") which will then be used for allocating device memory inside the solver.

The object should be created via [`cudssDataCreate()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdatacreate "cudssDataCreate") and destroyed via [`cudssDataDestroy()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdatadestroy "cudssDataDestroy").

During execution of any of the stages [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute"), configuration settings of the solver are read from `cudssConfig_t` and thus affect the execution and internal data stored in the `cudssData_t` object.

Data parameters can be updated or retrieved by calling [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet") or [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") respectively.

cudssConfig_t.doc:
The structure stores configuration settings for the solver. This object is a lightweight (host-side) wrapper around common solver settings. While it can be re-used for solving different linear systems, it is recommended to have one per linear system.

The object should be created via [`cudssConfigCreate()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssconfigcreate "cudssConfigCreate") and destroyed via [`cudssConfigDestroy()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssconfigdestroy "cudssConfigDestroy").

During execution of any of the stages [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute"), configuration settings of the solver are read from `cudssConfig_t` and thus affect the execution.

Configuration settings can be updated or retrieved by calling [`cudssConfigSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssconfigset "cudssConfigSet") or [`cudssConfigGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssconfigget "cudssConfigGet") respectively.
Note: certain settings need to be set before a corresponding solver stage is executed (e.g., reordering algorithm must be set prior to the phase [`cudssPhase_t::CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS`]).

cudssDeviceMemHandler_t.doc:
This structure holds information about the user-provided, stream-ordered device memory pool (mempool).

The object can be created by setting the struct members described below.

Once created, a device memory handler can be set for the cuDSS library handle via [`cudssSetDeviceMemHandler()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudsssetdevicememhandler "cudssSetDeviceMemHandler").

Once set for the cuDSS library handle, information about the set device memory handler can be retrieved via [`cudssGetDeviceMemHandler()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssgetdevicememhandler "cudssGetDeviceMemHandler").

`char name[CUDSS_ALLOCATOR_NAME_LEN]`

The name of the provided mempool (must not exceed 64 characters).

ctx.doc: A pointer to the user-owned mempool/context object.

device_alloc.signature: int device_alloc(void * ctx, void * * ptr, size_t size, cudaStream_t stream)
device_alloc.doc:
A function pointer to the user-provided routine for allocating device memory of size on `stream`.

The allocated memory should be made accessible to the current device (or more precisely, to the current CUDA context bound to the library handle).

This interface supports any stream-ordered memory allocator `ctx`. Upon success, the allocated memory can be immediately used on the given stream by any operations enqueued/ordered on the same stream after this call.

It is the caller’s responsibility to ensure a proper stream order is established.

The allocated memory should be at least 256-byte aligned.

ctx.doc: A pointer to the user-owned mempool object.

ptr.doc: On success, a pointer to the allocated buffer.

size.doc: The amount of memory in bytes to be allocated.

stream.doc: The CUDA stream on which the memory is allocated (and the stream order is established).

return_value.doc: The error status (as `int`) of the invocation. Must return 0 on success and any nonzero integer otherwise.

device_free.signature: int device_free(void * ctx, void * ptr, size_t size, cudaStream_t stream)
device_free.doc:
A function pointer to the user-provided routine for deallocating device memory of `size` on `stream`.

This interface supports any stream-ordered memory allocator. Upon success, any subsequent accesses (of the memory pointed to by the pointer `ptr`)
ordered after this call are undefined behaviors.

It is the caller’s responsibility to ensure a proper stream order is established.

If the arguments `ctx` and `size` are not the same as those passed to `device_alloc` to allocate the memory pointed to by `ptr`, the behavior is undefined.

The argument `stream` need not be identical to the one used for allocating `ptr`, as long as the stream order is correctly established. The behavior is undefined if this assumption is not held.

ctx.doc: A pointer to the user-owned mempool object.

ptr.doc: The pointer to the allocated buffer.

size.doc: The size of the allocated memory.

stream.doc: The CUDA stream on which the memory is deallocated (and the stream order is established).

return_value.doc: The error status (as `int`) of the invocation. Must return 0 on success and any nonzero integer otherwise.

cudssPinnedMemHandler_t.doc:
This structure holds information about the user-provided pinned (page-locked) host memory pool (mempool).

It mirrors [`cudssDeviceMemHandler_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdevicememhandler-t "cudssDeviceMemHandler_t"), but for pinned host memory.

The object can be created by setting the struct members described below.

Once created, a pinned host memory handler can be set for the cuDSS library handle via [`cudssSetPinnedMemHandler()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudsssetpinnedmemhandler "cudssSetPinnedMemHandler").

Once set for the cuDSS library handle, information about the set pinned host memory handler can be retrieved via [`cudssGetPinnedMemHandler()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssgetpinnedmemhandler "cudssGetPinnedMemHandler").

`char name[CUDSS_ALLOCATOR_NAME_LEN]`

The name of the provided mempool (must not exceed 64 characters).

ctx.doc:
A pointer to the user-owned mempool/context object.

Any allocation properties (for example, the flags passed to `cudaHostAlloc()` / `cudaHostRegister()`, or a huge-page / parallel pre-fault policy) are carried by `ctx` and are thus fixed for a given handler instance. The allocation routine may still dispatch internally based on `size` (for example, a registered huge-page path for large requests versus a `cudaHostAlloc()` path for small ones).

pinned_alloc.signature: int pinned_alloc(void * ctx, void * * ptr, size_t size, cudaStream_t stream)
pinned_alloc.doc:
A function pointer to the user-provided routine for allocating pinned host memory of `size` bytes.

The stream is the CUDA stream the data object is bound to (see [`cudssSetStream()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudsssetstream "cudssSetStream")). Synchronous host allocators may ignore it; stream-aware allocators may use it to establish ordering with work enqueued by cuDSS.

This routine must return pinned host memory, for example from `cudaHostAlloc()` or from ordinary host memory that this routine registers with `cudaHostRegister()` before returning. cuDSS treats the returned pointer as already pinned and does not call `cudaHostRegister()`/`cudaHostUnregister()` for it; it only tracks the buffer internally so the same `size` value can be passed back to `pinned_free`.

If the allocator uses a threading runtime internally for parallel pre-faulting before `cudaHostRegister()`, make sure it is compatible with any threading runtime used by a cuDSS threading layer in the same process.

ctx.doc: A pointer to the user-owned mempool object.

ptr.doc: On success, a pointer to the allocated buffer.

size.doc: The amount of memory in bytes to be allocated.

stream.doc: The CUDA stream the data object is bound to (see [`cudssSetStream()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudsssetstream "cudssSetStream")).

return_value.doc: The error status (as `int`) of the invocation. Must return 0 on success and any nonzero integer otherwise.

pinned_free.signature: int pinned_free(void * ctx, void * ptr, size_t size, cudaStream_t stream)
pinned_free.doc:
A function pointer to the user-provided routine for deallocating the pinned host memory of `size` bytes pointed to by `ptr`.

The `size` argument is the same value that was passed to `pinned_alloc()`, which makes size-aware releases (for example, `cudaHostUnregister()` followed by `munmap()`) possible.

If the arguments `ctx` and `size` are not the same as those passed to `pinned_alloc` to allocate the memory pointed to by `ptr`, the behavior is undefined.

The argument `stream` need not be identical to the one used for allocating `ptr`, as long as the stream order is correctly established. The behavior is undefined if this assumption is not held.

ctx.doc: A pointer to the user-owned mempool object.

ptr.doc: The pointer to the allocated buffer.

size.doc: The size of the allocated memory.

stream.doc: The CUDA stream on which the memory is deallocated.

return_value.doc: The error status (as `int`) of the invocation. Must return 0 on success and any nonzero integer otherwise.

cudssLoggerCallback_t.doc: A callback function pointer type for logging.

functionName.doc: Name of the API function that generated the log.

cudaDataType_t.doc:
The CUDA data type enumerator (from `library_types.h`) specifies the data type of values, offsets and indices used in cuDSS matrix objects and API calls.

cuDSS accepts the `cudaDataType_t` values `CUDA_R_32F`, `CUDA_R_64F`, `CUDA_C_32F`, `CUDA_C_64F` (matrix values) and `CUDA_R_32I`, `CUDA_R_64I` (indices and offsets), and defines the following additional values and aliases.

CUDSS_R_64F_MP2.doc: cuDSS-specific value (experimental): 128-bit real double-double floating-point, stored as the unevaluated sum of two normalized `double` values (hi + lo); see [Double-double values (CUDSS_R_64F_MP2)](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#double-double-values-cudss-r-64f-mp2). `CUDSS_R_64F_64F` is a deprecated alias of this value.

CUDSS_R_32I.doc: Alias of `CUDA_R_32I`: 32-bit signed integer (`int32_t`). Used for index and offset arrays.

CUDSS_R_64I.doc: Alias of `CUDA_R_64I`: 64-bit signed integer (`int64_t`). Used for index and offset arrays. It does not lift the limit of $2^{31}$ on the number of rows and columns.

CUDSS_DATA_TYPE_UNSET.doc: cuDSS-specific sentinel value indicating an uninitialized or unset data type. Not a valid value for user-facing API calls.

cudssStatus_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies possible status values (on the host) which can be returned from calls to cuDSS routines.

Note: device side failures are returned via [`CUDSS_DATA_INFO`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_INFO") from [`cudssDataParam_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "cudssDataParam_t").

CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED.doc: One of the input operands was not properly initialized prior to the call to a cuDSS routine. This can usually be one of the opaque objects like [`cudssHandle_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsshandle-t "cudssHandle_t"), [`cudssData_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdata-t "cudssData_t") or others.

CUDSS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED.doc:
A resource allocation failed. This is usually caused by a device or host allocation
failure, and can also report a CUDA memory allocation error observed at a public API
boundary.

CUDSS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE.doc: An incorrect value or parameter was passed to the function (a negative vector size, or a NULL pointer for a must-have buffer, for example).

CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: An unsupported (but otherwise reasonable) parameter was passed to the function.

CUDSS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED.doc: The GPU program failed to execute, or a non-allocation CUDA error was pending at a public API boundary.

CUDSS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR.doc: An internal cuDSS operation failed, including an unexpected C++ exception.

CUDSS_STATUS_IR_FAILED.doc: Iterative refinement failed to meet the requested convergence tolerance. In this case, the iterations were performed and the refined solution is still accessible.

cudssConfigParam_t.doc: The enumerator specifies possible names of solver configuration settings. For each setting there is a matching type to be used in [`cudssConfigSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssconfigset "cudssConfigSet") or [`cudssConfigGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssconfigget "cudssConfigGet").

CUDSS_CONFIG_REORDERING_ALG.doc:
Algorithm for the reordering phase. Supported options are:

* [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_DEFAULT`] - let the library choose (typically nested dissection).
* [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION`] - a customized nested dissection algorithm based on METIS.
* [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] - a custom combination of block triangular reordering and COLAMD algorithms which can be used together with global pivoting to increase solution pivots.
  When this option is used for reordering, cuDSS uses an appropriate custom factorization algorithm (without the need to change the factorization setting [`CUDSS_CONFIG_FACTORIZATION_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_FACTORIZATION_ALG")).
* [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] - similar to [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] in that it implies using a special factorization algorithm which is tailored for a block-triangular representation but uses a trivial block structure.
* [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD`] - an approximate minimum degree (AMD) reordering.
* [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NONE`] - uses natural (identity) order for the internal ordering when no user permutation is supplied.

Note: [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] and [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] are only supported for general (non-symmetric or non-hermitian) matrices.

Note: [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] uses an upper bound on the number of non-zero entries in the factors.
If this bound appears to be not sufficient during the factorization phase, a runtime device error is returned (which can be checked by synchronizing the stream and calling `cudssDataGet()` with [`CUDSS_DATA_INFO`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_INFO") which will output the device error).
In order to set a non-default upper bound, one should call `cudssConfigSet()` with [`CUDSS_CONFIG_MAX_LU_NNZ`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_MAX_LU_NNZ") setting.

Note: [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD`] does not support the matrix index type `int64_t`.

Associated parameter type: [`cudssReorderingAlg_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "cudssReorderingAlg_t")

Default value: [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_DEFAULT`].

CUDSS_CONFIG_FACTORIZATION_ALG.doc:
Algorithm for the factorization phase. Supported options are:

* [`cudssFactorizationAlg_t::CUDSS_FACTORIZATION_ALG_DEFAULT`] - the default factorization algorithm.
  This option chooses the best fitting factorization algorithm based on the choice of the reordering algorithm and sparsity structure produced by it.
  It is not recommended to use other options.
* [`cudssFactorizationAlg_t::CUDSS_FACTORIZATION_ALG_MULTIBLOCK`] - multiblock factorization algorithm. Starting with cudss 0.8.0, this option is supported only for real double data type. Suggested for use with extremely sparse matrices.
* [`cudssFactorizationAlg_t::CUDSS_FACTORIZATION_ALG_GENERAL`] - general factorization algorithm.

Associated parameter type: [`cudssFactorizationAlg_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssfactorizationalg-t "cudssFactorizationAlg_t")

Default value: [`cudssFactorizationAlg_t::CUDSS_FACTORIZATION_ALG_DEFAULT`].

CUDSS_CONFIG_SOLVE_ALG.doc:
Algorithm for the solving phase. Supported options are:

* [`cudssSolveAlg_t::CUDSS_SOLVE_ALG_DEFAULT`] - the default solve algorithm.
* [`cudssSolveAlg_t::CUDSS_SOLVE_ALG_GENERAL`] - triangular solve only (forward/back substitution using existing L/U factors, without modifying them).

Associated parameter type: [`cudssSolveAlg_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsssolvealg-t "cudssSolveAlg_t")

Default value: [`cudssSolveAlg_t::CUDSS_SOLVE_ALG_DEFAULT`], currently equivalent to [`cudssSolveAlg_t::CUDSS_SOLVE_ALG_GENERAL`].

CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG.doc:
Algorithm for pivot epsilon calculation. When a pivot has magnitude smaller than the pivot epsilon threshold (see the description of [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_EPSILON`]), it is replaced by an appropriately signed value derived from the epsilon; the chosen algorithm controls how that value is computed.

Supported options are:

* [`cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_DEFAULT`] - Default behavior pre-selected by the library, currently equivalent to [`cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_STATIC`].
* [`cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_SCALED`] - Pivots with magnitude smaller than epsilon will be replaced by the appropriately signed epsilon scaled by the maximum element in the corresponding row and column of the original matrix.
* [`cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_STATIC`] - Pivots with magnitude smaller than epsilon will be replaced by the appropriately signed epsilon (no scaling).

Note: [`cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_SCALED`] is not supported when [`CUDSS_CONFIG_REORDERING_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_REORDERING_ALG") is set to [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`].

Associated parameter type: [`cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivotepsilonalg-t "cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t")

Default value: [`cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_DEFAULT`].

CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG.doc:
Matching is an optional preprocessing step which computes a permutation to put larger values on the diagonal which often improves the accuracy of the solution.
This permutation is then combined with the permutation from the reordering.
Set to [`CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatchingalg-t "CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE") to disable matching; for any other value, matching is enabled.
While matching often reduces the number of perturbed pivots and improves accuracy of the solution
(especially for ill-conditioned and badly scaled matrices) there are no guarantees that the accuracy will improve.
Enabling matching brings an overhead during the analysis step and changes the non-zero pattern of the factors and therefore, can slow down factorization and solve.

For matrix types other than [`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_GENERAL`] ([`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_SYMMETRIC`], [`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_HERMITIAN`], [`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_SPD`], [`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_HPD`]), matching preserves the matrix symmetry by default.
Use [`CUDSS_CONFIG_FORCE_NONSYMMETRIC_MATCHING`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_FORCE_NONSYMMETRIC_MATCHING") to force the non-symmetric matching path for these matrix types.

When [`CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN") is selected, symmetry-preserving
matching also derives 2x2 pivot candidates and keeps each candidate’s columns
consecutive during nested-dissection reordering. This does not force a 2x2 numerical
pivot; the Bunch-Kaufman test still selects 1x1 or 2x2 pivots from the reordered
matrix. This combination requires
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION"), a single process (which may
use multiple GPUs), and no user permutation or user nested-dissection partition tree.
Forcing non-symmetric matching in this combination is not supported.

Note: matching routines require their internal workspace size to fit into the limit of 32-bit integers. The workspace limit depend on the choice of the matching algorithm.
The biggest requirement among them is to have `10 * nrows + nnz` < `INT_MAX` (`nrows` and `nnz` for the input matrix without accounting for symmetry).

Supported options are:

* [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE`] - matching is disabled.
* [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_COUNT`] - this option is based on `job = 1` from MC64 algorithm (HSL).
  Computes a column permutation of the matrix so that the permuted matrix has as many entries on its diagonal as possible. The values on the diagonal are of arbitrary size.
  Note: this option does not use matrix values and thus can actually make the accuracy worse. It is not recommended to use this algorithm for matching unless there is a justified need.
* [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_MIN_DIAG`] - this option is based on `job = 2` from MC64 algorithm (HSL). Computes a column permutation of the matrix so that the smallest value on the diagonal of the permuted matrix is maximized.
* [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_MIN_DIAG_ALT`] - this option is based on `job = 3` from MC64 algorithm (HSL). Computes a column permutation of the matrix so that the smallest value on the diagonal of the permuted matrix is maximized.
  This algorithm is different from the one used for [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_MIN_DIAG`].
* [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_SUM`] - this option is based on `job = 4` from MC64 algorithm (HSL). Computes a column permutation of the matrix so that the sum of the diagonal entries of the permuted matrix is maximized.
* [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_PRODUCT`] - this option is based on `job = 5` from MC64 algorithm (HSL). Computes a column permutation of the matrix so that the product of the diagonal entries of the permuted matrix is maximized.
  In addition, this algorithm computes the row/col scaling vectors which can further improve accuracy of the solution.
* [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_AUTO`] - the library selects the alg to apply. For [`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_SPD`] and [`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_HPD`] matrices this resolves to [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE`]; for all other matrix types it resolves to [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_PRODUCT`] (matching with scaling, the most robust option). Since [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_PRODUCT`] requires matrix values, [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_AUTO`] falls back to [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE`] when values are not provided during analysis, rather than failing.

Note: one of the options, [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_PRODUCT`], computes scaling vectors in addition to the matching permutation. This option is considered to be the most impactful and it is recommended to use this option if accuracy of the solution needs to be improved.
However, this option requires matrix values to be present during the analysis step.

Matching is not supported with:

* non-uniform batches;
* uniform-batch settings ([`CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE") greater
  than 1 or [`CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX") other than -1);
* [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD") or
  [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD");
* Schur complement mode;
* [`CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_SCALED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivotepsilonalg-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_SCALED");
* more than $2^{30}$ nonzeros with 32-bit matrix indices.

During reordering, [`CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_AUTO`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatchingalg-t "CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_AUTO") disables matching
for these combinations instead of failing; an explicitly enabled matching
algorithm returns [`CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED").
Later configuration changes do not trigger AUTO fallback and can return
[`CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED"). Rerun analysis after changing
options that affect matching compatibility.

With an effective [`CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN") pivot type,
[`CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_AUTO`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatchingalg-t "CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_AUTO") disables matching when it is incompatible
with the Bunch-Kaufman matching requirements above. See
[`CUDSS_PIVOT_AUTO`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_AUTO") for pivot-selection fallback rules.

Distributed inputs have additional requirements when matching runs.
When row ranges do not overlap, they must cover the matrix without gaps
in ascending rank order. With 32-bit matrix offsets, the sum of local nonzero
counts must fit in `INT32_MAX`. Violations return
[`CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED"), including when matching was
selected by [`CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_AUTO`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatchingalg-t "CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_AUTO"), without falling back to
no matching.

For matrices with type [`CUDSS_R_64F_MP2`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudadatatype-t "CUDSS_R_64F_MP2"), value-dependent matching algorithms
evaluate magnitudes in double precision after summing the `hi` and `lo` components.
Consequently, matching can ignore value differences that are representable in double-double
precision but not in double precision, which can affect the selected permutation in edge
cases. Scaling factors are also computed in double precision and are therefore less accurate
than scaling factors computed in full double-double precision. Scaling vectors returned
through [`CUDSS_DATA_SCALE_ROW`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_SCALE_ROW") and [`CUDSS_DATA_SCALE_COL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_SCALE_COL") use
the double-double layout ([Double-double values (CUDSS_R_64F_MP2)](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#double-double-values-cudss-r-64f-mp2)), with the double-precision scaling value stored in `hi` and
`lo` set to zero.

Associated parameter type: [`cudssMatchingAlg_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatchingalg-t "cudssMatchingAlg_t")

Default value: [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_AUTO`].

CUDSS_CONFIG_FORCE_NONSYMMETRIC_MATCHING.doc:
Controls whether matching for matrix types other than [`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_GENERAL`] ([`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_SYMMETRIC`], [`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_HERMITIAN`], [`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_SPD`], [`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_HPD`]) should preserve symmetry or use the non-symmetric matching path.
Set to `0` to preserve symmetry when matching is enabled for these matrix types.
Set to `1` to force non-symmetric matching for these matrix types.
This setting has no effect when matching is disabled. With
[`CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_AUTO`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatchingalg-t "CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_AUTO"), matching is disabled for SPD/HPD matrices
and enabled for symmetric/Hermitian indefinite matrices when values are available
during analysis, subject to the compatibility restrictions in
[`CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG").
Setting it to `1` together with [`CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN") while matching is
explicitly enabled (a non-`AUTO` [`CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG") value) is not supported;
if both come from their `AUTO` defaults, matching falls back to disabled instead of failing.

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `0` (preserve symmetry).

CUDSS_CONFIG_SOLVE_MODE.doc:
Modifier on the system matrix used during the solve phase.

| Value | Solved system | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`CUDSS_SOLVE_MODE_NORMAL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsssolvemode-t "CUDSS_SOLVE_MODE_NORMAL") | $A x = b$ | Default. |
| [`CUDSS_SOLVE_MODE_TRANSPOSE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsssolvemode-t "CUDSS_SOLVE_MODE_TRANSPOSE") | $A^T x = b$ | No effect for [`CUDSS_MTYPE_SYMMETRIC`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatrixtype-t "CUDSS_MTYPE_SYMMETRIC") and [`CUDSS_MTYPE_SPD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatrixtype-t "CUDSS_MTYPE_SPD") because $A = A^T$. |
| [`CUDSS_SOLVE_MODE_CONJUGATE_TRANSPOSE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsssolvemode-t "CUDSS_SOLVE_MODE_CONJUGATE_TRANSPOSE") | $A^H x = b$ | Supported for GENERAL complex matrices. No effect for complex [`CUDSS_MTYPE_HERMITIAN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatrixtype-t "CUDSS_MTYPE_HERMITIAN") and [`CUDSS_MTYPE_HPD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatrixtype-t "CUDSS_MTYPE_HPD") because $A = A^H$. |

Associated parameter type: [`cudssSolveMode_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsssolvemode-t "cudssSolveMode_t")

Default value: [`CUDSS_SOLVE_MODE_NORMAL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsssolvemode-t "CUDSS_SOLVE_MODE_NORMAL").

For matrix types [`CUDSS_MTYPE_SYMMETRIC`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatrixtype-t "CUDSS_MTYPE_SYMMETRIC") and [`CUDSS_MTYPE_SPD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatrixtype-t "CUDSS_MTYPE_SPD")
the transposed solve is a no-op ($A = A^T$).

For complex matrix types [`CUDSS_MTYPE_HERMITIAN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatrixtype-t "CUDSS_MTYPE_HERMITIAN") and
[`CUDSS_MTYPE_HPD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatrixtype-t "CUDSS_MTYPE_HPD"), the conjugate-transposed solve is a no-op
($A = A^H$).

Transpose solve returns [`CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED") in the following cases:

* matrix types [`CUDSS_MTYPE_HERMITIAN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatrixtype-t "CUDSS_MTYPE_HERMITIAN") and [`CUDSS_MTYPE_HPD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatrixtype-t "CUDSS_MTYPE_HPD")
  because they satisfy $A = A^H$, not necessarily $A = A^T$;
* together with the Schur complement (a non-zero [`CUDSS_CONFIG_SCHUR_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_SCHUR_MODE"));
* together with BTF / COLAMD reordering ([`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`]
  or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`]);
* for non-uniform matrix batches (`batchCount > 0` matrix objects).

Conjugate-transpose solve returns [`CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED") for real data
types and for non-GENERAL matrix types except [`CUDSS_MTYPE_HERMITIAN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatrixtype-t "CUDSS_MTYPE_HERMITIAN") and
[`CUDSS_MTYPE_HPD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatrixtype-t "CUDSS_MTYPE_HPD"). It otherwise shares the same Schur complement,
BTF / COLAMD, and non-uniform matrix-batch restrictions as transpose solve.

CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS.doc:
Maximum number of steps during the iterative refinement. Refer to [`CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL") for the details.

Note: In-place iterative refinement is not supported in deterministic mode, for
non-uniform batch solves, or in MGMN mode unless both the right-hand side and
solution are distributed matrices. It is supported for uniform batches, including
with [`CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX") and with
[`CUDSS_DATA_UBATCH_MASK`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_UBATCH_MASK").

Note: for a uniform batch the convergence check is evaluated on a single system –
the first system selected by the current selection – and the resulting decision to
stop, together with the reported number of steps actually taken, applies to the whole
batch. Entries other than that one do not take part in the
[`CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL") comparison.

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `0`.

CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL.doc:
Iterative refinement tolerance.

When users set both [`CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS") > 0 and [`CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL") > 0,
the solver performs iterative refinement with convergence checking.

In each iteration, the relative residual norm is computed as $||r||_2 / ||b||_2$ where $r = b - Ax$.

The refinement terminates early if the residual norm is less than the specified tolerance.

If [`CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL") = 0 and [`CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS") > 0,
exactly [`CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS") iterations are performed without convergence checking.

The actual number of iterations performed can be retrieved via [`CUDSS_DATA_IR_N_STEPS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_IR_N_STEPS").
If the tolerance is not met after all iterations, [`CUDSS_STATUS_IR_FAILED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_IR_FAILED") is returned.

Associated parameter type: `double`

Default value: `0.0` (tolerance checking disabled).

CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_TYPE.doc:
Type of pivoting

The exact meaning of this parameter depends on the choice of the reordering algorithm which can be changed through [`CUDSS_CONFIG_REORDERING_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_REORDERING_ALG").
For [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] and [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] the parameter refers to the global pivoting, while for [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION`] and others it refers to the partial pivoting procedure (1x1 pivots, or 1x1 and 2x2 pivots with [`CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN")).

Note that in the latter case, if the matrix type is symmetric but not positive-definite, then the pivoting is also symmetric and the pivot is searched for within the diagonal of the block (by default via Bunch-Kaufman, see [`CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN")), if only the pivot type is not equal to [`cudssPivotType_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_NONE`].

cuDSS resolves the effective pivot type during the reordering phase. Changing this
parameter after reordering does not change the analyzed solver data; the new value
takes effect on the next [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute") call that includes
[`CUDSS_PHASE_REORDERING`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_REORDERING").

For more details, see the description of the [pivoting strategies](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#numerical-pivoting).

Associated parameter type: [`cudssPivotType_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "cudssPivotType_t")

Default value: [`cudssPivotType_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_AUTO`].

CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_THRESHOLD.doc:
Pivoting threshold $p_{threshold}$ which is used to determine if diagonal element is subject to pivoting and will be swapped with the maximum element in the row (or column) depending on the [type of pivoting](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t).
The diagonal element will be swapped if:
$p_{threshold} \cdot max_{(sub)row \\, or \\, col} |a_{ij}| \geq |a_{ii}|$

For more details, see the description of the [pivoting strategies](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#numerical-pivoting).

Note: for the global pivoting strategies this parameter is only supported when the reordering algorithm is set to [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD") or [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD").

Note: when [`CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN") is selected, this parameter overrides the Bunch-Kaufman $\alpha$ constant that decides between a 1x1 and a 2x2 pivot. The value must be finite and in the range $0 < \alpha \le 1$; otherwise [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute") returns [`CUDSS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE"). The default Bunch-Kaufman value $\alpha = (1 + \sqrt{17}) / 8 \approx 0.64$ is used when this parameter has not been set explicitly. Explicitly setting the parameter to `1.0` uses $\alpha = 1$.

Associated parameter type: `double`

Default value: `1.0`.

CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_EPSILON.doc:
Pivoting epsilon.

By default, this is the absolute value to test and replace small diagonal elements encountered during numerical factorization.

In case [`CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG") is set to [`cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_SCALED`], this value will be additionally scaled (see more details in the description of [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG`]).

Associated parameter type: `double`

Default value: `1e-5` for single precision and `1e-13` for double precision.

CUDSS_CONFIG_MAX_LU_NNZ.doc:
Upper limit on the number of nonzero entries in LU factors. This is only relevant for non-symmetric matrices and reordering algorithm set to [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`].
If the number of non-zero entries in L and U exceeds the set limit, a runtime error occurs. See also the note for [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] in the table entry for [`CUDSS_CONFIG_REORDERING_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_REORDERING_ALG").

Associated parameter type: `int64_t`

Default value: `-1` (then the parameter value is ignored and cuDSS uses an estimate of `100 nnz` where `nnz` is the number of non-zero entries in the input matrix).

CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE.doc:
Memory mode: `0` (default = device-only) or `1` (hybrid = host/device).

Note: Hybrid host/device memory mode should be enabled before the analysis phase ([`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute") with [`CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS")).
If the decision to use the hybrid mode is done after the analysis phase, the hybrid memory mode should be enabled and analysis phase must be re-done (which is sub-optimal).

Note: Unlike the hybrid host/device execution mode (see [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE")) which controls where compute kernels are executed, the hybrid memory mode
only allows cuDSS to keep a part of the factor values (internal data) on the host and always uses the GPU for factorization and solve.

For more details, see [Hybrid host/device memory mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-memory-mode) feature.

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `0` (disabled).

Currently not supported when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] is used for reordering, or, when [`cudssFactorizationAlg_t::CUDSS_FACTORIZATION_ALG_MULTIBLOCK`] is used for the factorization.

CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_DEVICE_MEMORY_LIMIT.doc:
User-defined device memory limit (number of bytes) for the hybrid memory mode.

This setting only affects execution when the hybrid host/device memory mode is enabled.
For more details, see [Hybrid host/device memory mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-memory-mode) feature.

Note: In case of multiple devices ([`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg")), this value must be set for each device separately by calling `cudaSetDevice()` prior to [`cudssConfigSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssconfigset "cudssConfigSet").

Associated parameter type: `int64_t`

Default value: `-1` (use the internal default heuristic).

CUDSS_CONFIG_USE_CUDA_REGISTER_MEMORY.doc:
A flag to enable or disable usage of `cudaHostRegister()` by cuDSS hybrid host/device memory mode. Since the hybrid memory mode of cuDSS uses host memory to store the factors,
it can use `cudaHostRegister()` (if the HW supports it) to speedup associated host-to-device and device-to-host memory transfers.
However, registering host memory has limitations and in some cases might lead to slowdowns. If the flag is set to `0`, cuDSS will not attempt to use `cudaHostRegister()` even if the HW supports it.
If a [`cudssPinnedMemHandler_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspinnedmemhandler-t "cudssPinnedMemHandler_t") is attached with [`cudssSetPinnedMemHandler()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudsssetpinnedmemhandler "cudssSetPinnedMemHandler"), registration of routed host allocations is controlled by the handler instead of this flag. Therefore, a pinned host memory handler is not supported when this flag is set to `0`.
This setting only affects execution when the hybrid memory mode is enabled. For more details, see [Hybrid host/device memory mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-memory-mode) feature.

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `1` (use `cudaHostRegister()` if the device supports it).

CUDSS_CONFIG_HOST_NTHREADS.doc:
Number of threads to be used by cuDSS in [MT mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-threaded-mt-mode).
This setting only affects execution when the multi-threaded mode is enabled.

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `-1` (use number of threads returned by `cudssGetMaxThreads()`).

CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE.doc:
Execute mode: `0` (default = device-only) or `1` (hybrid = host/device).
Hybrid execute mode allows cuDSS to perform calculations on both GPU and CPU.
Currently it is used to speed up execution parts with low parallelization capacity.

Note: Reordering part of the analysis step is performed on CPU regardless of execute mode value.

Note: Hybrid execute mode should be enabled before the analysis phase ([`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute") with [`cudssPhase_t::CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS`]).

Note: Unlike the hybrid execution mode which controls where compute kernels are executed
(and allows greater flexibility in placement of the input data), the hybrid host/device memory mode [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE") only allows cuDSS to keep part of the factor values (internal data)
on the host while only the GPU is used for factorization and solve.

Note: The input matrix can be passed with host memory pointers regardless of this setting. If hybrid execute mode
is enabled, right hand side and solution can be host memory pointers as well (single-process runs with `nrhs` = 1 only).

For more details, see the [Hybrid host/device execute mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-execute-mode) feature.

Associated parameter type: `int`

Note: For `nrhs > 1`, the analysis phase must be run with `nrhs > 1`, i.e. the right-hand side passed to [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute") with [`CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS") must have `nrhs > 1`; otherwise a later solve with `nrhs > 1` can return [`CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED"). The host/device placement of the factorization and solve kernels is decided during analysis and takes `nrhs` from that right-hand side. The `nrhs` of subsequent solves does not need to match.

Note: It is strongly recommended to enable the threading layer ([`cudssSetThreadingLayer()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudsssetthreadinglayer "cudssSetThreadingLayer")) when hybrid execute mode is active, as all analysis step computations are enhanced by multi-threading. Expect significant performance improvements, especially for small and medium-sized matrices.

Default value: `0` (disabled). Currently not supported when [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE") is used.
Also not supported when [`CUDSS_CONFIG_DETERMINISTIC_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_DETERMINISTIC_MODE") is enabled, or, when `batchCount` is greater than 1, or when right-hand side and/or solution have a non-trivial leading dimension.

CUDSS_CONFIG_ND_NLEVELS.doc:
Minimum number of levels for the nested dissection reordering. The value for this parameter should be a positive integer.
In [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode) and [MG mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-mg-mode), cuDSS automatically increases the effective number of levels for an internally generated partition tree, if needed, to satisfy $2^{n_{levels}-1} \geq \max(n_{proc}, n_{device})$, where $n_{proc}$ is the number of processes and $n_{device}$ is the number of devices. The configuration getter continues to return the configured value.
When [`CUDSS_DATA_USER_ND_PARTITION_TREE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_USER_ND_PARTITION_TREE") is provided, the configured number of levels must already provide at least one leaf per process or device; cuDSS does not enlarge a user-provided tree.
This setting only works when reordering algorithm is [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION`] (which is also [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_DEFAULT`]).

Note: This is considered an advanced performance knob and it is recommended to use a non-default value only when optimizing for performance. Typical values to try should not be too far from the default value, e.g. from the range 8 - 11.

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `10`.

CUDSS_CONFIG_ND_UBFACTOR.doc:
Controls the balance of the nested dissection partition tree. The value represents the allowed percentage of imbalance between the two children at each level of the partition tree. Possible values are from 1 to 100.

Note: Smaller values produce a more balanced partition tree. For [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode) and [MG mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-mg-mode), it is recommended to use smaller values in the range 2 to 5.

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `20`.

CUDSS_CONFIG_EMULATION_MANTISSA_BIT_COUN.doc:
Enables floating-point emulation in cuDSS and controls the working precision in bits of mantissa.
The value is the number of significand bits that the emulation must preserve. The original input
data type (e.g. [`CUDSS_R_64F`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudadatatype-t "CUDSS_R_64F") or [`CUDSS_C_64F`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudadatatype-t "CUDSS_C_64F")) and the format of the
produced factors are not changed; only the internal kernels switch to an emulated path.

When this setting is `0` (default), emulation is disabled and cuDSS uses the regular floating-point
kernels. When set to a positive integer $b$, cuDSS uses emulated kernels that reproduce the
result with at least $b$ bits of mantissa precision. For example, to recover a near full
double-precision result (FP64 mantissa is 52 bits), values in the range of `53` to `55` are typical;
smaller values trade accuracy for performance.

Note: this is a performance/accuracy tuning knob. Larger values produce more work, while smaller
values are faster but less accurate. Some of the accuracy lost to a smaller value can typically be
recovered by enabling iterative refinement via [`CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS") (and
optionally [`CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL")).

Note: emulation kernels are used only during the factorization phase. Other phases (analysis, solve,
iterative refinement) continue to use the regular floating-point kernels.

Note: this setting is ignored on GPUs with compute capability 8.0 or earlier
and on GPUs with compute capability 9.0.

Note: emulation is currently supported for double precision real ([`CUDSS_R_64F`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudadatatype-t "CUDSS_R_64F")) and
double precision complex ([`CUDSS_C_64F`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudadatatype-t "CUDSS_C_64F")) data types.

Note: emulation is not supported with [`CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN")
when superpanels are formed.

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `0` (emulation disabled).

CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE.doc:
The number of matrices in a uniform batch of systems to be processed by cuDSS. Uniform batch of matrices is defined as a batch of matrices with the same non-zero pattern but potentially different values.
To create a uniform batch of matrices (unlike a non-uniform batch) one can simply use the usual [`cudssMatrixCreateCsr()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssmatrixcreatecsr "cudssMatrixCreateCsr") or [`cudssMatrixCreateDn()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssmatrixcreatedn "cudssMatrixCreateDn")
with the only change: as a pointer to the matrix values one should provide a buffer which holds values for all matrices in the batch.
Thus, it should have `nnz * CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE` elements
for sparse matrices (`csr_values` only) and `nrows * ncols * CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE` elements for dense matrices.

Note: a single system can be viewed as a uniform batch with [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE`] set to 1.

Combining this parameter with matrices created by the non-uniform batch APIs returns
[`CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED").

There are two ways how cuDSS can process a uniform batch based on the value of the [`CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX"): either factorizing (or solving) all matrices at once or just one at a time.

Benchmark factorization and solve separately when choosing a batch size: their performance crossover points can differ with the matrix and GPU.

For details, see the description of [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX`].

Note: [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE`] must be set before calling [`cudssPhase_t::CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS`].

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `1`.

Currently not supported when either [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE") (see [here](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-memory-mode)) or [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE") (see [here](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-execute-mode))
are enabled, or [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode) is used, or with [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] and [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] reordering algorithms.

CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX.doc:
`-1` or a 0-based index of matrix in a uniform batch which will be processed during factorization or solve phase.
Special value of `-1` can be used to tell cuDSS to process all matrices in the uniform batch at once.

The value must be less than [`CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE"). It can be set after
[`CUDSS_PHASE_FACTORIZATION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_FACTORIZATION"), which is how a whole-batch factorization is
followed by solves of individual systems.

Combining this parameter with matrices created by the non-uniform batch APIs returns
[`CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED").

When [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX`] is set, cuDSS treats the input sparse matrix, right-hand
side and solution as regular matrices with just one set of values. This allows a uniform
batch to be processed one system at a time while re-using the result of the analysis and
keeping the factors of all the matrices in a single `cudssData_t` object.

The two phases differ in which descriptors cuDSS offsets by [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX`]:

| Descriptor | [`CUDSS_PHASE_FACTORIZATION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_FACTORIZATION") | [`CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE") |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sparse matrix | Not offset. The caller points the descriptor at item `k`. | Not used. |
| Factors | Written to slot `k`. | Read from slot `k` (internal). |
| Right-hand side, solution | Not offset; a single system. | Not offset; a single system. |

Note: because the factorization does not offset the matrix values, leaving the matrix
descriptor at the base storage of the batch factorizes item `0` into slot `k`, and the
following solve then returns item `0`’s answer with a success status. To factorize batch
item `k`, point the matrix descriptor at item `k` first, for example with
`cudssMatrixSetValues()`.

A solve may only cover systems that have factors. A factorization performed with
[`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX`] set to `k` gives factors to item `k` alone, so a subsequent
solve with [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX`] reset to `-1` is rejected with
[`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`]: the remaining items were never factorized. Factorize the
whole batch, or keep the solve narrowed to the items that were.

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `-1`

Currently not supported when either [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE") (see [here](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-memory-mode)) or [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE") (see [here](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-execute-mode))
are enabled, or [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode) is used, or with [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] and [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] reordering algorithms.

CUDSS_CONFIG_USE_SUPERPANELS.doc:
Use superpanel optimization: `1` (default = enabled) or `0` (disabled).

Note: superpanel optimization should be enabled before the analysis phase ([`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute") with [`CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS")).
If the decision to use the superpanel optimization mode is done after the analysis phase, the superpanel optimization should be enabled and analysis phase must be re-done which is sub-optimal).

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `1` (enabled).

CUDSS_CONFIG_DEVICE_COUNT.doc:
Device count in case of multiple device (see [`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg"))

Note: Maximum supported device count is 16.
Set this parameter before [`CUDSS_CONFIG_DEVICE_INDICES`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_DEVICE_INDICES").

See [`CUDSS_CONFIG_DEVICE_INDICES`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_DEVICE_INDICES") for how this parameter is matched against
multi-GPU handles (`device_count > 1`).

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `1`.

CUDSS_CONFIG_DEVICE_INDICES.doc:
A list of device indices as an integer array of length [`CUDSS_CONFIG_DEVICE_COUNT`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_DEVICE_COUNT").

Note: Device indices must be unique and in the range 0 to `cudaGetDeviceCount()` - 1.
Setting this parameter initializes the CUDA runtime (via `cudaGetDeviceCount`) and can
return [`CUDSS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED") if that call fails.
[`CUDSS_CONFIG_DEVICE_COUNT`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_DEVICE_COUNT") must be set before this parameter;
for [`cudssConfigSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssconfigset "cudssConfigSet"), `sizeInBytes` must equal `device_count * sizeof(int)`;
for [`cudssConfigGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssconfigget "cudssConfigGet"), `sizeInBytes` must be at least that large.
For multi-GPU handles (`device_count > 1` from [`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg")), if either this
parameter or [`CUDSS_CONFIG_DEVICE_COUNT`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_DEVICE_COUNT") is set, the resulting count and
ordered indices must match the handle. Single-device handles do not enforce that match.
If neither of them is set, [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute") uses the handle topology.
A `NULL` value is invalid for [`cudssConfigSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssconfigset "cudssConfigSet") (unlike [`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg"), where `NULL` selects `0..device_count-1`).

Associated parameter type: `int *` (array of [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_DEVICE_COUNT`] elements).

Default value: identity `0, 1, ..., device_count - 1` (after [`cudssConfigCreate()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssconfigcreate "cudssConfigCreate")).

CUDSS_CONFIG_SCHUR_MODE.doc:
Schur complement mode: `0` (default = disabled) or `1` (enabled).

For more details regarding the Schur complement feature, see [Schur complement feature](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#schur-complement).

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `0` (disabled).

Currently not supported when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] is used for reordering, when [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode) or [multi-GPU mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-mg-mode) is used,
or, when [`cudssFactorizationAlg_t::CUDSS_FACTORIZATION_ALG_MULTIBLOCK`] is used for the factorization. It is also not supported for uniform and non-uniform batches, or when matching is enabled.

CUDSS_CONFIG_DETERMINISTIC_MODE.doc:
Enable deterministic mode.
In deterministic mode, cuDSS is guaranteed to provide the bit-wise identical result at every run when executed on GPUs with the same architecture
and the same number of SMs (assuming the input data and solver settings are also bit-wise identical).

Note: in deterministic mode cuDSS uses a different set of kernels which often might be slower than the kernels used in the default mode.

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `0` (disabled).

Currently the feature is supported only for single-gpu, single rhs, and with both hybrid host/device memory mode ([`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE")) and hybrid host/device execute mode ([`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE")) disabled.
Uniform batches are not supported either: [`CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE") greater than 1 together with deterministic mode returns [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`].
Also, this feature does not support iterative refinement ([`CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS") greater than 0) or the reordering algorithms [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD") and [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD").
The deterministic-mode setting used during analysis is part of the analyzed state.
After analysis completes, changing this setting requires running analysis again;
otherwise factorization, refactorization, or solve returns
[`CUDSS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE").
Bunch-Kaufman pivoting does not support deterministic mode when superpanels are formed.

CUDSS_CONFIG_DOWNCAST_FACTORS.doc:
Controls whether cuDSS stores the double-precision factors in single (reduced) precision after factorization, releasing the full-precision factors. When disabled (the default) the factors are kept in full precision.

Supported values:

* [`CUDSS_DOWNCAST_FACTORS_MODE_DISABLED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdowncastfactorsmode-t "CUDSS_DOWNCAST_FACTORS_MODE_DISABLED") (default): disabled.
* [`CUDSS_DOWNCAST_FACTORS_MODE_KEEP_BLOCK_DIAGONAL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdowncastfactorsmode-t "CUDSS_DOWNCAST_FACTORS_MODE_KEEP_BLOCK_DIAGONAL"): store downcast factors and release the full-precision factors, retaining the full-precision diagonal block of every supernode.
* [`CUDSS_DOWNCAST_FACTORS_MODE_KEEP_STRICT_DIAGONAL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdowncastfactorsmode-t "CUDSS_DOWNCAST_FACTORS_MODE_KEEP_STRICT_DIAGONAL"): as above but retain only the full-precision strict diagonal (one value per column). With Bunch-Kaufman pivoting, the off-diagonal of each 2x2 diagonal block is also retained in full precision for mixed solves.

Numerical factorization is performed in the matrix value precision. Iterative refinement is also computed in the matrix value precision. The supported downcast conversions are [`CUDSS_R_64F`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudadatatype-t "CUDSS_R_64F") to [`CUDSS_R_32F`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudadatatype-t "CUDSS_R_32F") and [`CUDSS_C_64F`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudadatatype-t "CUDSS_C_64F") to [`CUDSS_C_32F`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudadatatype-t "CUDSS_C_32F").

It is possible to perform the entire solve phase in the downcast factor precision by providing right-hand side and solution matrices in the single-precision counterpart of the matrix value type. The right-hand side and solution value types must match. Transpose and conjugate-transpose solves are supported when the right-hand side and solution use the matrix value precision (mixed-precision solve), but not when they use the downcast factor precision.

For example, with a [`CUDSS_R_64F`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudadatatype-t "CUDSS_R_64F") matrix and downcast factors enabled:

* [`CUDSS_R_32F`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudadatatype-t "CUDSS_R_32F") right-hand side and solution matrices run the entire solve in single precision over the downcast factors.
* [`CUDSS_R_64F`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudadatatype-t "CUDSS_R_64F") right-hand side and solution matrices run a mixed-precision solve with double-precision arithmetic, single-precision off-diagonal factor sources, and retained double-precision diagonal factor sources.

The corresponding complex value types are [`CUDSS_C_64F`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudadatatype-t "CUDSS_C_64F") and [`CUDSS_C_32F`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudadatatype-t "CUDSS_C_32F"). Any other right-hand side and solution value type returns [`CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED") at the solve phase.

[`CUDSS_CONFIG_DOWNCAST_FACTORS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_DOWNCAST_FACTORS") must be set before the factorization phase and must remain unchanged through every solve that reuses those factors.

Associated parameter type: [`cudssDowncastFactorsMode_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdowncastfactorsmode-t "cudssDowncastFactorsMode_t")

Default value: [`CUDSS_DOWNCAST_FACTORS_MODE_DISABLED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdowncastfactorsmode-t "CUDSS_DOWNCAST_FACTORS_MODE_DISABLED").

Downcast factors are not supported in the following configurations:

* With [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD") or [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD").
* When [`CUDSS_CONFIG_DETERMINISTIC_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_DETERMINISTIC_MODE") is enabled.
* When [`CUDSS_CONFIG_SCHUR_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_SCHUR_MODE") is enabled.
* For transpose or conjugate-transpose solves when the right-hand side and solution use the downcast factor precision.

These unsupported configurations return [`CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED").

CUDSS_CONFIG_MEMORY_OPTIMIZATION_SETTING.doc:
Selects which memory optimizations cuDSS may apply. Each optimization trades some capability, or some other resource, for a lower memory footprint; none of them is applied unless it is requested here.

The value is a bitwise OR of the flags in [`cudssMemoryOptimizationFlags_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmemoryoptimizationflags-t "cudssMemoryOptimizationFlags_t"), which describes what each flag does and what it costs. The flags are independent and may be combined in any way; [`CUDSS_MEMORY_OPTIMIZATION_DEFAULT`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmemoryoptimizationflags-t "CUDSS_MEMORY_OPTIMIZATION_DEFAULT") (zero) requests none of them. Setting a value with any bit that does not correspond to a defined flag returns [`CUDSS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE") and leaves the configuration unchanged.

The values reported by [`CUDSS_DATA_MEMORY_ESTIMATES`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_MEMORY_ESTIMATES") are not affected by this setting: they describe the requirement before any optimization releases memory.

The setting takes effect for the factorization or refactorization phase during which it is set; setting it afterwards has no effect on a factorization that has already run.

Associated parameter type: [`cudssMemoryOptimizationFlags_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmemoryoptimizationflags-t "cudssMemoryOptimizationFlags_t")

Default value: [`CUDSS_MEMORY_OPTIMIZATION_DEFAULT`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmemoryoptimizationflags-t "CUDSS_MEMORY_OPTIMIZATION_DEFAULT").

cudssDataParam_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies possible parameter names which can set or get in the [`cudssData_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdata-t "cudssData_t") object. For each parameter name
there is an associated type to be used in [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet") or [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet"). Each parameter
name is marked with “in”, “out”, or “in, out” depending on whether a parameter can be only set, only retrieved, or both.

CUDSS_DATA_INFO.doc:
By default, this parameter can be used to detect device-side asynchronous errors (primarily, during factorization and solve).
However, in the special case, when in [hybrid host/device execute mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-execute-mode), factorization is done on the host at least partially,
this parameter can be used to retrieve host-side errors. In case execution is successful, the value is `0`.

Note: the error returned via [`cudssDataParam_t::CUDSS_DATA_INFO`] is independent from the host side status of type [`cudssStatus_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "cudssStatus_t") returned by all cuDSS routines, including [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute").
One of the noticeable use cases is when a matrix of the system is passed with an `mtype` for positive-definite matrices but it appears to have non-positive minors (at least numerically).
In this case, calling [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") with [`cudssDataParam_t::CUDSS_DATA_INFO`] after the factorization phase will return the 1-based index of the first encountered non-positive minor.
Then one can set the device error back to zero via [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet"), and either change the matrix type or adjust the matrix values (to make the matrix positive-definite) and call the factorization phase again.

Note that the returned index is 1-based and is for the reordered matrix.
To get the corresponding original index, first map it through the permutation returned by [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") for [`CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_ROW`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_ROW").
If symmetry-preserving matching is enabled, map that result through [`CUDSS_DATA_PERM_MATCHING`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_PERM_MATCHING") as well; in 0-based notation the combined mapping is `matching[reordering[index]]`.

Another case is [`CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN"): if the diagonal solve encounters 2x2 pivot metadata
which is internally inconsistent, the solve phase returns [`CUDSS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR") and sets
[`cudssDataParam_t::CUDSS_DATA_INFO`] to `1`. Unlike the non-positive minor above this value is not an index, and it indicates a
failure inside cuDSS rather than a property of the input matrix.

Direction: in, out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `int`.

CUDSS_DATA_LU_NNZ.doc:
