Number of non-zero entries in LU factors.

Note: in case `batchCount` > 1 (non-uniform batch) [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") returns accumulated number over all
matrices in the batch.

Direction: out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `int64_t`.

CUDSS_DATA_NPIVOTS.doc:
Number of perturbed 1x1 pivots during factorization. Stable, unperturbed 1x1 pivots
and 2x2 pivot blocks are not counted.

Direction: out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system.

CUDSS_DATA_INERTIA.doc:
Positive and negative indices of inertia for the system matrix `A` (two integer values). Valid only for symmetric/Hermitian non positive-definite matrix types.

Note: in case `batchCount` > 1 (non-uniform batch) [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") returns the accumulated number over all
matrices in the batch.

Direction: out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system.

CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_ROW.doc:
Row permutation `P` produced by the reordering algorithm. If matching is enabled,
this permutation applies to the matrix after [`CUDSS_DATA_PERM_MATCHING`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_PERM_MATCHING")
has been applied; it does not include the matching permutation.

For reordering algorithms other than [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD")
and [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD"), the row and column reordering
permutations are identical.

Note: using this parameter in [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") in case `batchCount` > 1 is not supported.

Direction: out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system.

CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_COL.doc:
Column permutation `Q` produced by the reordering algorithm. If matching is enabled,
this permutation applies to the matrix after [`CUDSS_DATA_PERM_MATCHING`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_PERM_MATCHING")
has been applied; it does not include the matching permutation.

For reordering algorithms other than [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD")
and [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD"), the row and column reordering
permutations are identical.

Note: using this parameter in [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") in case `batchCount` > 1 is not supported.

Direction: out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system.

CUDSS_DATA_PERM_ROW.doc:
Final row permutation P (includes effects of both reordering and pivoting) which is applied to the original right-hand side of the system in the form $b_{new} = b_{old} \circ P$

Note: using this parameter in [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") in case `batchCount` > 1 is not supported.

Direction: out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system

Currently supported only when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] is used for reordering.

CUDSS_DATA_PERM_COL.doc:
Final column permutation Q (includes effects of both reordering and pivoting) which is applied to transform the solution of the permuted system into the original solution $x_{old} = x_{new} \circ Q^{-1}$

Note: using this parameter in [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") in case `batchCount` > 1 is not supported.

Direction: out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system

Currently supported only when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] is used for reordering.

CUDSS_DATA_PERM_MATCHING.doc:
Matching permutation.
For non-symmetric matching, this is a column permutation `Q` such that `A[:,Q]` is reordered and then factorized.
For symmetry-preserving matching, this is a symmetric permutation applied to both rows and columns.

Direction: out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system.

CUDSS_DATA_DIAG.doc:
Diagonal of the factorized matrix. The diagonal is returned in the original matrix order, taking into account all permutations applied during matching, reordering, and pivoting.

Note: when matching with scaling is enabled, the returned diagonal values retain
that scaling.

Note: with Bunch-Kaufman pivoting, only the diagonal entries of `D` are returned;
off-diagonal entries of 2x2 pivot blocks are not included.

Note: when a Schur complement is requested ([`CUDSS_CONFIG_SCHUR_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_SCHUR_MODE") is set to `1`),
the rows/columns belonging to the Schur complement are not factorized,
so no diagonal values exist for them. The returned buffer still has `n` entries, and the entries corresponding to
the Schur complement are **left unmodified**. They are the rows/columns for which the caller set
[`CUDSS_DATA_USER_SCHUR_INDICES`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_USER_SCHUR_INDICES") to 1.

For a diagonal query using neither [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD")
nor [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD"), the CUDA device that is current
when [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") is called must belong to the cuDSS handle; otherwise
[`CUDSS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE") is returned.

With a Schur complement, a device output buffer must additionally belong to that current
CUDA device; otherwise [`CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED") is returned. This
output-buffer restriction applies only when a Schur complement is requested: without one,
the whole buffer is written and it may be host memory or memory on any device.

In MGMN mode, this query is collective. Every process must configure non-null host and
device communicators with the same participating processes and consistent ranks before
analysis, and keep them unchanged through the query. All processes must perform the same
operation: either query the required size or retrieve the value using that size. The output
is written only on rank 0.

Note: in case `batchCount` > 1 (non-uniform batch) [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") returns the accumulated values over all
matrices in the batch.

Direction: out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the values of the sparse matrix of the system.

CUDSS_DATA_SCALE_ROW.doc:
Row scaling the factorized matrix (corresponding to the rows of the original matrix)

Direction: out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: the real-valued counterpart of the sparse matrix value type
(`float`, `double`, or double-double, see [Double-double values (CUDSS_R_64F_MP2)](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#double-double-values-cudss-r-64f-mp2))

Only supported when matching is enabled (i.e. [`CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG") is not [`CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatchingalg-t "CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE")) and the chosen matching algorithm computes the scaling.
For symmetry-preserving matching, users should not assume that row and column scaling vectors are different.

CUDSS_DATA_SCALE_COL.doc:
Column scaling the factorized matrix (corresponding to the columns of the original matrix).

Direction: out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: the real-valued counterpart of the sparse matrix value type
(`float`, `double`, or double-double, see [Double-double values (CUDSS_R_64F_MP2)](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#double-double-values-cudss-r-64f-mp2)).

Only supported when matching is enabled (i.e. [`CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG") is not [`CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatchingalg-t "CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE")) and the chosen matching algorithm computes the scaling.
For symmetry-preserving matching, users should not assume that row and column scaling vectors are different.

CUDSS_DATA_USER_PERM.doc:
User permutation to be used instead of running the reordering algorithms.
The user permutation can be disabled by providing a `NULL` with zero size with [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet").
The provided buffer should be an integer array of size `n`, where `n` is the number of rows/columns of the system matrix.
The integer type must match the one used for the system matrix.
The values should represent a valid permutation vector for the set $\\{ index base, ..., n - 1 + index base \\}$

Note: after [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet") is called with [`cudssDataParam_t::CUDSS_DATA_USER_PERM`], the data are copied into an internal buffer so that the user buffer can be deallocated or re-used.

Note: using this parameter in [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") in case `batchCount` > 1 is not supported.

Direction: in, out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system

Currently not supported when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] is used for reordering.

Also not supported together with matching (i.e. [`CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG") other than [`CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatchingalg-t "CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE")), except for the [`CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN") symmetry-preserving matching path: matching computes its own row/column permutation, which cannot be composed with a user-supplied one.
With [`CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_AUTO`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatchingalg-t "CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_AUTO"), cuDSS resolves matching to [`CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatchingalg-t "CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE") instead of erroring; an explicitly requested matching algorithm returns [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`].

CUDSS_DATA_ND_PARTITION_TREE.doc:
Nested Dissection (ND) partition tree information, also known as a separator tree or separator sizes, which are computed during the reordering phase and used for improving parallelization.
The number of elements in this array is $2^{n_{levels}} - 1$ with
$n_{levels}$ from [`CUDSS_CONFIG_ND_NLEVELS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_ND_NLEVELS"). It can be used in combination with
[`CUDSS_DATA_USER_PERM`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_USER_PERM") and [`CUDSS_DATA_USER_ND_PARTITION_TREE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_USER_ND_PARTITION_TREE") for a matrix with the same sparsity structure.
This avoids regenerating the same reordering information while retaining the same performance for the factorization and solve phases.

See the [Nested Dissection Partition Tree](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#user-provided-nested-dissection-nd-partition-tree-data-saving-reordering) section for more details.

Direction: out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system.

CUDSS_DATA_USER_ND_PARTITION_TREE.doc:
User provided nested dissection (ND) partition tree information, which is used instead of running the reordering algorithm (therefore, saving runtime).
It must be used in combination with [`CUDSS_DATA_USER_PERM`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_USER_PERM") to have an effect.

See [`CUDSS_DATA_ND_PARTITION_TREE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_ND_PARTITION_TREE") for the size and usage information. The user ND partition tree can be disabled by providing a `NULL` with zero size with [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet").

In [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode) and [MG mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-mg-mode), the configured [`CUDSS_CONFIG_ND_NLEVELS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_ND_NLEVELS") must provide at least one leaf per process or device. cuDSS does not enlarge a user-provided partition tree.

Note: While it is possible to construct this array outside cuDSS (e.g., extracting the so-called `sizes` array from METIS / ParMETIS), we recommend to only use this feature by extracting the ND partition tree from cuDSS,
followed by passing it back in subsequent calls.

Direction: in, out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system.

CUDSS_DATA_MEMORY_ESTIMATES.doc:
Memory estimates (in bytes) for host and device memory required for the chosen memory mode.
The chosen memory mode is defined as the memory mode detected during the last executed analysis phase for the current `cudssData_t` object and the state of the corresponding `cudssConfigParam_t` object during the call.

See [`cudssConfigParam_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "cudssConfigParam_t") for more details.

Note: the returned memory estimate uses the input matrix, right-hand side, and solution descriptors and analysis-dependent settings captured during reordering or symbolic factorization. In particular, the estimate uses the number of right-hand sides, leading dimensions, batch or distributed formats, and user-provided RHS and solution buffer placement when the hybrid execute mode is enabled. For non-batch matrices, it also distinguishes an in-place solve, where the right-hand side and solution descriptors use the same value buffer, from an out-of-place solve. Analysis must be run again if these captured inputs change, including when switching between in-place and out-of-place solves. Changes to settings evaluated when the estimate is queried, such as iterative refinement or factor downcasting, are reflected by the next query and do not require another analysis.

Note: for uniform batches ([`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE`] greater than 1) cuDSS chooses between two
internal workspace layouts for the factorization, and the estimate reflects the layout that the
factorization is expected to use for the configuration as it stands at the time of the call. If
[`cudssDataParam_t::CUDSS_DATA_UBATCH_MASK`] is set, or [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE`] is changed, after the estimate has
been queried, the estimate may no longer describe the layout that will be used and should be
queried again. cuDSS may also fall back to the smaller layout if the larger one cannot be
allocated, in which case the factorization uses less memory than estimated.

Values returned in the output array at position:
\* 0 - permanent device memory
\* 1 - peak device memory
\* 2 - permanent host memory
\* 3 - peak host memory
\* 4 - minimum device memory required after analysis for hybrid factorization and solve
\* 5 - maximum host memory over analysis, factorization, and solve in hybrid memory mode
\* 6 - how far the analysis phase progressed when the estimate was produced (see below)
\* 7, … 15 - reserved for future use

Slots 4 and 5 model the hybrid memory path even when [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE") is disabled.

This query can be done once the non-zero count of the factors is known, and will return status [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`] if it cannot be processed.

The value at position 6 says how complete the estimate is, as one of [`cudssMemoryEstimateState_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmemoryestimatestate-t "cudssMemoryEstimateState_t").

Note: on multi-GPU ([`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg")) and multi-process runs the per-device factor counts only become available later in the analysis phase, so the query stays unavailable for longer than on a single-GPU run.

Note: in the multi-process (MGMN) mode this query is collective, including size probes with `sizeInBytes == 0`, and must be called by all ranks when inspecting an estimate after a failed [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute"). Every rank must request the same parameter, use the same query form, and provide valid local arguments. The same applies to [`CUDSS_DATA_HYBRID_DEVICE_MEMORY_MIN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_HYBRID_DEVICE_MEMORY_MIN").

Note: In case of multiple devices ([`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg")) memory estimate will be done for the calling device only.
Thus, `cudaSetDevice()` must be called prior to `cudssDataGet()` to get the memory estimate for the corresponding device.

Direction: out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `int64_t[16]`.

CUDSS_DATA_HYBRID_DEVICE_MEMORY_MIN.doc:
Minimal amount of device memory (number of bytes) required in the hybrid memory mode. This query must be done after the analysis phase and will return status [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`] if it cannot be processed. Unlike [`CUDSS_DATA_MEMORY_ESTIMATES`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_MEMORY_ESTIMATES"), this query is refused until the analysis phase has completed.

The returned value uses right-hand side and solution shapes. When the hybrid execute mode is enabled, it also uses user-provided RHS and solution buffer placement. For non-batch matrices, it also distinguishes an in-place solve, where the right-hand side and solution descriptors use the same value buffer, from an out-of-place solve. This information is captured during reordering or symbolic factorization. Analysis must be run again if these captured inputs change, including when switching between in-place and out-of-place solves. Changes to settings evaluated when the estimate is queried, such as iterative refinement or factor downcasting, are reflected by the next query and do not require another analysis. The query models the hybrid memory path even when [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE") is disabled.

Note: in the multi-process (MGMN) mode this query is collective, including size probes with `sizeInBytes == 0`. Every rank must request the same parameter, use the same query form, and provide valid local arguments.

Note: In case of multiple devices ([`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg")), minimal memory will be returned for the calling device only.
Thus, `cudaSetDevice()` must be called prior to `cudssDataGet()` to get the minimal memory for the corresponding device.

Direction: out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `int64_t`

For more details, see the [Hybrid host/device memory mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-memory-mode) feature.

CUDSS_DATA_FLOPS.doc:
Floating-point operation count for the factorization phase.

Note: the value is available after the [`CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS") step.

Direction: out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `int64_t`.

CUDSS_DATA_COMM_DEVICE.doc:
Device communicator for [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode).
The device and host communicators must agree in size and rank ordering.
The actual type of the communicator must match the device communication backend of the [communication layer](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#communication-layer-library-in-cudss) which must be set via calling [`cudssSetCommLayer()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudsssetcommlayer "cudssSetCommLayer").
This communicator is used for communication involving device memory buffers.

Note: [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet") stores the communicator pointer itself (the communicator is not copied), so it must remain valid until the parameter is set again or the [`cudssData_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdata-t "cudssData_t") object is destroyed.

Direction: in

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `void*`

See [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode) for further details.

CUDSS_DATA_COMM_HOST.doc:
Host communicator for [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode).
The actual type of the communicator must match the host communication backend of the [communication layer](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#communication-layer-library-in-cudss) which must be set via calling [`cudssSetCommLayer()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudsssetcommlayer "cudssSetCommLayer").
This communicator is used for communication involving host memory buffers.

Note: [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet") stores the communicator pointer itself (the communicator is not copied), so it must remain valid until the parameter is set again or the [`cudssData_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdata-t "cudssData_t") object is destroyed.

Direction: in

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `void*`

See [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode) for further details.

CUDSS_DATA_NSUPERPANELS.doc:
Number of superpanels in the matrix.

Direction: out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system.

CUDSS_DATA_USER_SCHUR_INDICES.doc:
User-provided Schur complement indices. The provided buffer should be an integer array of size `n`, where `n` is the number of rows (columns) of the system matrix,
and the integer type should match the one used for the system matrix.
The values should be equal to `1` for the rows/columns which are part of the Schur complement and `0` for the rest.

Note: after [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet") is called with [`cudssDataParam_t::CUDSS_DATA_USER_SCHUR_INDICES`], the data are copied into an internal buffer so that the user buffer can be deallocated or re-used.

Direction: in

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system.

CUDSS_DATA_SCHUR_SHAPE.doc:
Shape of the Schur complement matrix as a triplet `(nrows, ncols, sparse nnz)`. The last entry is only relevant when the Schur complement needs to be exported as a sparse matrix.
By querying with [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") with [`cudssDataParam_t::CUDSS_DATA_SCHUR_SHAPE`], users can get the necessary allocation sizes for the Schur complement buffers
which can then be used to create a `cudssMatrix_t` object and passed back to cuDSS to fill in the Schur complement data via [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") with [`CUDSS_DATA_SCHUR_MATRIX`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_SCHUR_MATRIX").

Direction: out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `int64_t[3]`.

CUDSS_DATA_SCHUR_MATRIX.doc:
Schur complement matrix as a `cudssMatrix_t` object.

Direction: out

Memory: host (with underlying buffers on host or device)

Associated parameter type: `cudssMatrix_t`

Note: the data type for matrix values, offsets and indices (if it is a sparse matrix) must be same as for the values, offsets and indices of the system matrix respectively.

Note: Schur complement matrix cannot be a distributed matrix. Also, Schur complement cannot be computed for matrix batches currently. For the dense Schur complement,
the layout must be column-major. For sparse Schur complement, the matrix type must be [`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_GENERAL`] and the matrix view must be [`cudssMatrixViewType_t::CUDSS_MVIEW_FULL`].

CUDSS_DATA_USER_HOST_INTERRUPT.doc:
User-provided host interrupt pointer. Setting this pointer to a non-`NULL` value enables user interruption of cuDSS routines on the host.
Specifically, in the calls to [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute") cuDSS will perform checks on the host for the value of the pointer.
If it is non-zero, execution stops and cuDSS returns early (before the phase execution completes) with the status [`CUDSS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED").
To resume after an interruption, set the value at that location back to `0` and call again.
To remove the (small) overhead of checking for the host interruption, the interruption can be completely disabled by setting [`cudssDataParam_t::CUDSS_DATA_USER_HOST_INTERRUPT`] to `NULL`.

Note: unlike the array parameters (e.g. [`CUDSS_DATA_USER_PERM`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_USER_PERM")), the pointer itself is stored and the pointed-to value is not copied by [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet").
The location must remain valid until the parameter is set again or the [`cudssData_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdata-t "cudssData_t") object is destroyed.

Note: since most of device kernels inside cuDSS are launched asynchronously,
execution on the GPU may continue some time after the host execution has been interrupted.

Direction: in

Memory: host

Default value: `NULL` (user interruption disabled)

Associated parameter type: pointer to a 4-byte integer (e.g. `int32_t` or `int`).

Note: When setting the flag from another thread, the user must use an atomic store with release semantics so the library observes the write. A plain write to a non-atomic object from another thread is a data race and undefined behavior.

Note: `std::atomic<int>` (C++) or `_Atomic(int)*` (C) may be used when the object representation is a single 4-byte integer; the library does not guarantee correct behavior for all atomic types.

Note: The host interruption feature is not supported when [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode) or [MG mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-mg-mode) is used.
Also, reordering algorithms [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] and [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] do not support the user interrupt currently.

CUDSS_DATA_IR_N_STEPS.doc:
Actual number of iterative refinement steps performed

Direction: out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `int`

This parameter stores the actual number of iterative refinement iterations performed during the solve phase.

The value can be less than [`CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS") if user-specified convergence tolerance is reached.
The value is 0 if iterative refinement is disabled or if the initial solution already satisfies the tolerance.

CUDSS_DATA_UBATCH_MASK.doc:
An array specifying the subset of problems to be processed in the uniform batch case, at factorization and at solve alike. It holds one `int` per problem in the batch, so its size must be `CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE * sizeof(int)`; a non-zero element includes the problem at that index in the operation, a zero element excludes it. Not supported for non-uniform matrix batches.

Note: [`cudssDataParam_t::CUDSS_DATA_UBATCH_MASK`] can be used as an alternative to [`CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX") to select multiple specific problems from the batch in a single call. The two are mutually exclusive.

Note: [`cudssDataParam_t::CUDSS_DATA_UBATCH_MASK`] applies to the factorization and the solve. At the solve the selected systems are solved as usual and every other entry of the solution is left exactly as the caller supplied it, neither solved nor zeroed. Clear the mask, by calling `cudssDataSet()` with a `NULL` value and a size of `0`, to solve the whole batch. A mask that selects no system at all is accepted and solves nothing.

Note: a solve may only select systems that have factors. cuDSS rejects the solve with [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`] when the mask selects a system that no factorization since the last [`CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS") covered.

Note: the mask must be set before [`CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS") or before the first factorization, as its internal device-side storage is allocated at that point. Introducing a mask after a factorization that ran without one is not supported. This applies to a mask intended only for the solve as well: set one (an all-ones mask selects the whole batch) before the analysis, then narrow it when the solve is issued.

Note: the problems excluded by the mask keep the factors computed for them by a previous factorization; only the selected problems are refreshed. A mask that selects no problems at all is accepted and refreshes nothing, leaving all previously computed factors intact.

Note: a solve without a mask covers the whole batch and therefore requires every problem to have been factorized. cuDSS accumulates the masks of all factorizations performed since the last [`CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS"), so factorizing the batch in several masked chunks and then solving once is supported. A solve that would cover a problem no factorization ever selected returns [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`], since there are no factors to solve it with; setting a mask on the solve narrows both what is solved and what is therefore required.

Note: when [`CUDSS_CONFIG_DOWNCAST_FACTORS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_DOWNCAST_FACTORS") is enabled, the mask must select a single contiguous range of problems, and the value reported by [`CUDSS_DATA_MEMORY_ESTIMATES`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_MEMORY_ESTIMATES") depends on the mask that is set when the estimate is queried. The transient full-precision factors are sized for the selected range, so querying with a narrow selection and then factorizing a wider one under-reports the peak. Query the estimate with the widest selection you intend to use.

Note: the mask can be retrieved with [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") once the data object has been used in a call to [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute").

Direction: in, out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `int *` (array of [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE`] elements).

Default value: `NULL` (no mask; all problems selected).

Not supported when [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE") or
[`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE") is enabled, in
[MG mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-mg-mode) or [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode),
or with [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD") or
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD").

cudssPhase_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies the solver phases to be performed in the main cuDSS routine [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute").
Phases can be combined with the binary OR operator (`|`) to specify multiple phases at once: `CUDSS_PHASE_FACTORIZATION | CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE`.

CUDSS_PHASE_SYMBOLIC_FACTORIZATION.doc:
Symbolic factorization

Note: it is not allowed to call symbolic factorization twice without calling the reordering phase in-between.

CUDSS_PHASE_REFACTORIZATION.doc:
Numerical re-factorization.

Note: For now it is only used if the reordering algorithm is set to [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`]. Otherwise, it is the same as FACTORIZATION phase.

Note: this phase returns [`CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED") if
[`CUDSS_MEMORY_OPTIMIZATION_SOLVE_ONLY`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmemoryoptimizationflags-t "CUDSS_MEMORY_OPTIMIZATION_SOLVE_ONLY") was set for the preceding factorization.

CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE_FWD_PERM.doc:
Applying reordering permutation to the right hand side before the forward solve (forward substitution).

Note: solve sub-phases are not supported when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] are used for reordering.

CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE_FWD.doc:
Forward substitution sub-step of the solving phase.

Note: this phase includes the local permutation due to the partial pivoting.
To remove this effect, if undesired, one can use a combination of reordering and final permutation (see [`CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_ROW`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_ROW") and [`CUDSS_DATA_PERM_ROW`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_PERM_ROW")).

Note: solve sub-phases are not supported when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] are used for reordering.

CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE_DIAG.doc:
Diagonal solve sub-step of the solving phase (only needed for symmetric/Hermitian matrix types).

Note: solve sub-phases are not supported when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] are used for reordering.

CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE_BWD.doc:
Backward substitution sub-step of the solving phase.

Note: this phase includes the local permutation due to the partial pivoting.
To remove this effect, if undesired, one can use a combination of reordering and final permutation (see [`CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_ROW`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_ROW") and [`CUDSS_DATA_PERM_ROW`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_PERM_ROW")).

Note: solve sub-phases are not supported when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] are used for reordering.

CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE_BWD_PERM.doc:
Applying inverse reordering permutation to the intermediate solution after the backward solve (backward substitution).
If matching (and scaling) is enabled, this phase also includes applying the inverse matching permutation and inverse scaling (as the matching permutation and scalings were used to modify the matrix before the factorization).

Note: solve sub-phases are not supported when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] are used for reordering.

CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE_REFINEMENT.doc:
Iterative refinement (see configuration settings [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS`] and [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL`]).

Note: solve sub-phases are not supported when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] are used for reordering.

CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE.doc:
Full solving phase, combining all of the above (forward permutation + forward solve + diagonal solve + backward solve + backward permutation) and (optional) iterative refinement.

Note: combining the solve sub-phases should be preferred to calling sub-phases separately.

Note: Changing the sparse matrix for this phase is allowed but with restrictions, see limitations for [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute").

cudssMatrixFormat_t.doc: The enumerator specifies the underlying matrix formats inside a cuDSS matrix object.

CUDSS_MFORMAT_DENSE.doc: Matrix is dense (applied to a single matrix and a batch equally).

CUDSS_MFORMAT_CSR.doc:
Matrix is in CSR format (applies to a single matrix and a batch equally)

Note: Only 3-array CSR is supported.

CUDSS_MFORMAT_BATCH.doc: Matrix object represents a batch of matrices.

CUDSS_MFORMAT_DISTRIBUTED.doc:
> Matrix object represents a distributed matrix (used in [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode))

Note: The format flags can be combined. E.g., creating a `cudssMatrix_t`
via [`cudssMatrixCreateBatchCsr()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssmatrixcreatebatchcsr "cudssMatrixCreateBatchCsr") would set both
[`cudssMatrixFormat_t::CUDSS_MFORMAT_CSR`] and [`cudssMatrixFormat_t::CUDSS_MFORMAT_BATCH`] flags. One can check for a mixture of flags via bit-wise operations, e.g.
`CUDSS_MFORMAT_CSR | CUDSS_MFORMAT_BATCH` for a batch of CSR matrices.

cudssMatrixType_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies available matrix types for sparse matrices.
Matrix type should be used to describe the properties of the underlying matrix storage.
Matrix type affects the decision about what type of factorization is computed by the solver.
E.g, when matrix type is one of the positive-definite types, checks for singular values on the diagonal is not done.

CUDSS_MTYPE_GENERAL.doc: General matrix [default] `LDU` factorization will be computed with optional local or global pivoting.

CUDSS_MTYPE_SYMMETRIC.doc: Real or complex symmetric matrix. `LDL^T` factorization will be computed with optional local pivoting.

CUDSS_MTYPE_HERMITIAN.doc: Complex Hermitian matrix. `LDL^H` factorization will be computed with optional local pivoting.

CUDSS_MTYPE_SPD.doc:
Symmetric positive-definite matrix Cholesky factorization will be computed with optional local pivoting

Note: if the matrix passed with this matrix type appears to have zero minors (at least numerically), one can get the 1-based index of the first encountered non-positive minor by
calling [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") with [`CUDSS_DATA_INFO`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_INFO"). As this would be a device-side error, the call to `cudssExecute()` may still return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`].

CUDSS_MTYPE_HPD.doc:
Hermitian positive-definite matrix Complex Cholesky factorization will be computed with optional local pivoting

Note: if the matrix passed with this matrix type appears to have zero minors (at least numerically), one can get the 1-based index of the first non-positive minor by
calling [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") with [`CUDSS_DATA_INFO`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_INFO"). As this would be a device-side error, the call to `cudssExecute()` may still return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`].

cudssMatrixViewType_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies available matrix view types for sparse matrices. Matrix view defines how the matrix is treated by
the main cuDSS routine [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute"). E.g., to provide only upper-triangle data for a symmetric matrix
one can use as [`CUDSS_MTYPE_SYMMETRIC`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatrixtype-t "CUDSS_MTYPE_SYMMETRIC") as matrix type combined with [`CUDSS_MVIEW_UPPER`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatrixviewtype-t "CUDSS_MVIEW_UPPER") as the matrix view.
If the accompanying matrix type is [`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_GENERAL`], the matrix view is ignored.

CUDSS_MVIEW_LOWER.doc: Lower-triangular matrix (including the diagonal). All values above the main diagonal will be ignored.

CUDSS_MVIEW_UPPER.doc: Upper-triangular matrix (including the diagonal). All values below the main diagonal will be ignored.

cudssIndexBase_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies indexing base (0 or 1) for sparse matrix indices (row start/end offsets and column indices).
Once set for a sparse matrix, [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute")
will use the indexing base from the input sparse matrix for all index-related data (e.g. output from
[`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") called with [`CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_ROW`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_ROW") or [`CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_COL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_COL")).

cudssLayout_t.doc: The enumerator specifies dense matrix layout.

cudssReorderingAlg_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies the reordering algorithm for the analysis phase.

Used with [`CUDSS_CONFIG_REORDERING_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_REORDERING_ALG").

CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_DEFAULT.doc:
The default algorithm for reordering (equivalent to
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION")).

CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD.doc: Block triangular form (BTF) combined with COLAMD. Supports global pivoting.

CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD.doc: COLAMD with trivial block structure. Supports global pivoting.

CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION.doc: Nested dissection algorithm based on METIS.

CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NONE.doc: Uses natural (identity) order for the internal ordering when no user permutation is supplied.

cudssFactorizationAlg_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies the factorization algorithm for the numerical factorization phase.

Used with [`CUDSS_CONFIG_FACTORIZATION_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_FACTORIZATION_ALG").

CUDSS_FACTORIZATION_ALG_DEFAULT.doc: The default factorization algorithm (equivalent to [`cudssFactorizationAlg_t::CUDSS_FACTORIZATION_ALG_GENERAL`], recommended).

CUDSS_FACTORIZATION_ALG_MULTIBLOCK.doc: Multiblock factorization algorithm. Supported only for real double data type ([`CUDSS_R_64F`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudadatatype-t "CUDSS_R_64F")). Suggested for use with extremely sparse matrices.

cudssSolveAlg_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies the algorithm for the solve phase.

Used with [`CUDSS_CONFIG_SOLVE_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_SOLVE_ALG").

CUDSS_SOLVE_ALG_DEFAULT.doc: Let the library choose the solve algorithm (recommended).

CUDSS_SOLVE_ALG_GENERAL.doc: Triangular solve only: forward/back substitution using the existing L/U factors without modifying them.

cudssSolveMode_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies which system matrix modifier is used in the solve phase.

Used with [`CUDSS_CONFIG_SOLVE_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_SOLVE_MODE").

cudssMemoryEstimateState_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies how complete a memory estimate is, i.e. how far the analysis phase
had progressed when it was produced.

Returned at position 6 of [`CUDSS_DATA_MEMORY_ESTIMATES`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_MEMORY_ESTIMATES").

CUDSS_MEMORY_ESTIMATE_STATE_NONE.doc:
Internal state before the non-zero count of the factors is known; it is never returned at
position 6. A query in this state returns [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED`] before the first
[`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute") call on the data object, and after one that failed early enough to
leave it unusable; otherwise it returns [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`]. In particular, an
estimate is **not**
available after the reordering phase alone: until the fill-in is known any number would
exclude the factors, which dominate the requirement.

CUDSS_MEMORY_ESTIMATE_STATE_FILL_KNOWN.doc:
Positions 0-3 include the factors, but the estimate is preliminary because later analysis
steps have not sized every workspace. When a
`cudssData_t` object is reused, it can also include allocation capacity retained from its
preceding analysis. Do not interpret this value as either a lower or an upper bound. On multi-GPU
([`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg")) and multi-process runs this state is only reached once the
per-device split exists, and positions 0-3 then hold that per-device requirement.
Positions 4-5 (the hybrid memory mode minimums) are reported as `0` below
[`CUDSS_MEMORY_ESTIMATE_STATE_FINAL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmemoryestimatestate-t "CUDSS_MEMORY_ESTIMATE_STATE_FINAL").

CUDSS_MEMORY_ESTIMATE_STATE_FINAL.doc: The analysis phase completed and positions 0-5 are the final estimate.

cudssDowncastFactorsMode_t.doc:
Selects how cuDSS keeps the numeric factors after factorization. By default ([`CUDSS_DOWNCAST_FACTORS_MODE_DISABLED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdowncastfactorsmode-t "CUDSS_DOWNCAST_FACTORS_MODE_DISABLED")) the factors are kept in full precision. The KEEP modes instead store the factors in single (reduced) precision and release the full-precision factors.

Used with [`CUDSS_CONFIG_DOWNCAST_FACTORS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_DOWNCAST_FACTORS").

CUDSS_DOWNCAST_FACTORS_MODE_DISABLED.doc: Keep the factors in full precision (no downcasting).

CUDSS_DOWNCAST_FACTORS_MODE_KEEP_BLOCK_D.doc: Store the factors in reduced (single) precision and release the full-precision factors, retaining the full-precision diagonal block of every supernode.

CUDSS_DOWNCAST_FACTORS_MODE_KEEP_STRICT_.doc: Store the factors in reduced (single) precision and release the full-precision factors, retaining only the full-precision strict diagonal (one value per column). With Bunch-Kaufman pivoting, the off-diagonal of each 2x2 diagonal block is also retained in full precision for mixed solves.

cudssMemoryOptimizationFlags_t.doc:
Flags naming the memory optimizations cuDSS may apply. The flags are independent and are combined with a bitwise OR; they are not positions on a scale, and new flags may be added without changing the meaning of the existing ones.

Used with [`CUDSS_CONFIG_MEMORY_OPTIMIZATION_SETTING`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_MEMORY_OPTIMIZATION_SETTING").

CUDSS_MEMORY_OPTIMIZATION_DEFAULT.doc: No additional memory optimizations are applied.

CUDSS_MEMORY_OPTIMIZATION_SOLVE_ONLY.doc:
Declares that the factors will not be recomputed, so the state which only a further factorization would read is released at the end of the factorization phase instead of being held through the solve. Solve phase performance may be slower.

A subsequent [`CUDSS_PHASE_FACTORIZATION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_FACTORIZATION") or [`CUDSS_PHASE_REFACTORIZATION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_REFACTORIZATION") on the same [`cudssData_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdata-t "cudssData_t") returns [`CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED"); running [`CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS") again makes factorization legal once more. Any number of solves may still be performed. The refusal depends on whether the state was actually released, not on the current setting, so clearing the flag afterwards does not lift it.

Unsupported configurations are:

* A partial uniform-batch factorization using [`CUDSS_DATA_UBATCH_MASK`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_UBATCH_MASK") or [`CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX"), because the state released after the first pass is what the remaining passes would need.
* [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD") or [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD") reordering.

These configurations return [`CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED") from [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute").

Eligible single-GPU, single-process, in-core symmetric-family configurations may release additional solve state. After it has been released, changing the configuration to require an incompatible solve path returns [`CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED").

cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies the algorithm for pivot epsilon calculation when replacing small pivots during numerical factorization.

Used with [`CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG").

CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_DEFAULT.doc: The default pivot epsilon algorithm (same as [`cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_STATIC`], recommended).

CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_SCALED.doc: Pivots below the threshold are replaced by the appropriately signed epsilon scaled by the maximum element in the corresponding row and column of the original matrix. Not supported with [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD") or [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD").

CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_STATIC.doc: Pivots below the threshold are replaced by the appropriately signed epsilon (no scaling). Recommended for most cases.

cudssMatchingAlg_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies the matching algorithm.

Used with [`CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG"). Except for [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE`] and [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_AUTO`], all options are based on the MC64 algorithm (HSL).

For matrix types other than [`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_GENERAL`] ([`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_SYMMETRIC`], [`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_HERMITIAN`], [`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_SPD`], [`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_HPD`]), matching preserves symmetry by default.

CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_AUTO.doc: Same as [`CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_PRODUCT`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatchingalg-t "CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_PRODUCT") (the most robust option). Matching with scaling; requires matrix values during analysis.

CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_COUNT.doc: Column permutation to maximize the number of diagonal entries (values arbitrary). MC64 JOB=1. Does not use matrix values; not recommended unless justified.

CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_MIN_DIAG.doc: Column permutation to maximize the smallest value on the diagonal. MC64 JOB=2.

CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_MIN_DIAG_ALT.doc: Alternate algorithm to maximize the smallest value on the diagonal. MC64 JOB=3. May differ in performance from [`CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_MIN_DIAG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatchingalg-t "CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_MIN_DIAG").

CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_SUM.doc: Column permutation to maximize the sum of diagonal entries. MC64 JOB=4.

CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_PRODUCT.doc: Column permutation to maximize the product of diagonal entries; also computes row/column scaling so that nonzero diagonal entries are 1 in absolute value and off-diagonal entries are ≤ 1. MC64 JOB=5. Most impactful for accuracy; requires matrix values during analysis.

cudssPivotType_t.doc: The enumerator specifies the pivoting strategy for numerical factorization.

CUDSS_PIVOT_AUTO.doc:
Automatic pivoting strategy [default]. Automatically selects the appropriate
pivot type based on the reordering algorithm and matrix type:

* For [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION"),
  [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD"), and
  [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NONE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NONE"):

  + Symmetric/Hermitian indefinite matrices: Uses [`CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN")
```text
whenever it is supported for the requested configuration (see below); otherwise
falls back to [`CUDSS_PIVOT_DIAGONAL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_DIAGONAL")
```
  + General matrices: Uses [`CUDSS_PIVOT_LOCAL_BLOCK`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_LOCAL_BLOCK")
  + SPD/HPD matrices: Uses [`CUDSS_PIVOT_DIAGONAL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_DIAGONAL") (numerical pivoting is
effectively disabled, since the matrix type indicates no pivoting is needed)
* For [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD") and [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD"):
  Uses [`CUDSS_PIVOT_GLOBAL_COL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_GLOBAL_COL")

Unlike an explicit [`CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN") request, AUTO never fails
due to a rejected combination in Symmetric/Hermitian indefinite matrices: it falls back to
[`CUDSS_PIVOT_DIAGONAL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_DIAGONAL") instead of selecting
[`CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN") whenever the requested configuration
includes batching ([`CUDSS_DATA_NSUPERPANELS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_NSUPERPANELS")-style non-uniform batching,
or uniform batching combined with [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE")/
[`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE")), an explicitly requested matching
algorithm that would not use the Bunch-Kaufman symmetry-preserving matching path (see
[`CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN")), or
[`CUDSS_CONFIG_DETERMINISTIC_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_DETERMINISTIC_MODE")/[`CUDSS_CONFIG_EMULATION_MANTISSA_BIT_COUNT`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_EMULATION_MANTISSA_BIT_COUNT")
combined with superpanels enabled. See [`CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN") for the
full list of restrictions that still apply when it is requested explicitly.

CUDSS_PIVOT_NONE.doc:
No pivoting. Used only with reordering algorithms
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION") and
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD") (MetisND and AMD).

CUDSS_PIVOT_GLOBAL_COL.doc:
Global column pivoting. Used only with reordering algorithms
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD") and [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD").
Searches for pivot elements within entire columns of the sub-matrix.

CUDSS_PIVOT_GLOBAL_ROW.doc:
Global row pivoting. Used only with reordering algorithms
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD") and [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD").
Searches for pivot elements within entire rows of the sub-matrix.

CUDSS_PIVOT_DIAGONAL.doc:
Diagonal pivoting. Used only with reordering algorithms
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION") and
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD") (MetisND and AMD).
For symmetric/Hermitian indefinite matrices, searches for pivot elements
only within the diagonal of the supernode.

CUDSS_PIVOT_LOCAL_BLOCK.doc:
Complete block pivoting. Used only with reordering algorithms
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION") and
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD") (MetisND and AMD).
For general matrices, searches for pivot elements within the entire
diagonal block of the supernode.

CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN.doc:
Bunch-Kaufman pivoting for symmetric/Hermitian indefinite matrices. Unlike
[`CUDSS_PIVOT_DIAGONAL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_DIAGONAL"), which only searches the diagonal and perturbs
tiny pivots, Bunch-Kaufman additionally forms stable 2x2 diagonal pivot blocks, which
improves accuracy on indefinite matrices where a 1x1 diagonal pivot would be unstable.
The 1x1-vs-2x2 selection threshold is controlled by
[`CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_THRESHOLD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_THRESHOLD") (see its description).

Solves using this pivoting strategy are synchronous and cannot be stream-captured.

At each numerical pivot step, Bunch-Kaufman applies this test inside the current local
active block. For pivot position $j$, let
$\lambda = \max_{i>j} |a_{ij}|$, and let $r$ be the row where that maximum
is attained. If $|a_{jj}| \ge \alpha \lambda$, cuDSS uses a 1x1 pivot at
$j$. Otherwise it computes $\sigma = \max_{k \ge j, k \ne r} |a_{rk}|$.
If $|a_{jj}| \sigma \ge \alpha \lambda^2$, cuDSS again uses a 1x1 pivot at
$j$; else if $|a_{rr}| \ge \alpha \sigma$, it interchanges $r$
with $j$ and uses a 1x1 pivot. In the remaining case, it interchanges
$r$ next to $j$ and forms a 2x2 pivot block.

The number of perturbed 1x1 pivots can be queried after factorization via
[`CUDSS_DATA_NPIVOTS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_NPIVOTS").

The following combinations are currently rejected with
[`CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED"):

* matrix types other than [`CUDSS_MTYPE_SYMMETRIC`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatrixtype-t "CUDSS_MTYPE_SYMMETRIC") and
  [`CUDSS_MTYPE_HERMITIAN`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssmatrixtype-t "CUDSS_MTYPE_HERMITIAN");
* reordering algorithms other than
  [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION"),
  [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD") (MetisND and AMD), or
  [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NONE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NONE");
* non-uniform batches;
* hybrid memory or hybrid execute mode with
  [`CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE") greater than 1;
* deterministic mode when superpanels are formed;
* fp64 emulation ([`CUDSS_CONFIG_EMULATION_MANTISSA_BIT_COUNT`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_EMULATION_MANTISSA_BIT_COUNT") > 0)
  when superpanels are formed.

Hybrid execute mode disables superpanel creation, so a request that combines hybrid execute
mode and [`CUDSS_CONFIG_USE_SUPERPANELS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_USE_SUPERPANELS") is not rejected by the superpanel
restriction unless [`CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE") is greater than 1.
Bunch-Kaufman supports all placements supported by hybrid execute mode.

When matching is enabled, Bunch-Kaufman additionally requires symmetry-preserving
matching, [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION"), a single process,
and no user permutation or user nested-dissection partition tree. A single process
may use multiple GPUs.

cudssDistributedInterface_t.doc:
This struct defines all communication primitives which need to be implemented
in (any) implementation of cuDSS communication layer, see for more details
[communication layer](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#communication-layer-library-in-cudss) and [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode).

**Dual-backend structure**: Each communication primitive must be implemented **twice** —
once for device (GPU) memory buffers (function pointer name ending in `Device`) and once
for host (CPU) memory buffers (function pointer name ending in `Host`). Both variants have
identical signatures. cuDSS selects the appropriate variant based on the memory location of the
buffers at call time. For example, rank query has two function pointers: `cudssCommRankDevice`
and `cudssCommRankHost`.

Note: the `comm` argument to all functions is interpreted by the implementation based on the
underlying communication backend. E.g., for OpenMPI it should be treated as an `MPI_Comm`.

Note: functions with a `stream` argument must be stream-ordered. For GPU-aware backends like
OpenMPI, this implies performing an explicit `cudaStreamSynchronize()` inside the implementation.

rank.doc: Rank of the calling process in the communicator.

return_value.doc: The error status (as `int`) of the invocation. Must return 0 on success and any nonzero integer otherwise.

cudssCommSizeDevice.doc: Function pointers to a routine which returns the number of processes in a communicator.

Function pointers to a routine which performs a broadcast from the `root` process

cudssThreadingInterface_t.doc:
This struct defines all threading primitives which need to be implemented

in (any) implementation of cuDSS threading layer, see for more details

[threading layer](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#threading-layer-library-in-cudss) and [MT mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/1.0.0/advanced_features.html#multi-threaded-mt-mode).

cudssGetMaxThreads.doc:
A function pointer to a routine which returns the maximum number of threads on the CPU
that can be used by cuDSS for parallel execution.

return_value.doc: The maximum number of threads on the CPU that can be used by cuDSS for parallel execution.

cudssParallelFor.signature: void cudssParallelFor(int nthr_requested, int ntasks, void * ctx, cudss_thr_func_t f)
cudssParallelFor.doc:
A function pointer to a routine which opens a `parallel for` section with the requested number of
threads and call cudss_thr_func_t (see `cudss_threading_interface.h` for details) `f` in
the for loop with ntasks number of iterations.

nthr_requested.doc: Requested number of threads for the parallel section.

ntasks.doc: Number of tasks in the parallel for loop.

ctx.doc:
A pointer to the input data for cudss_thr_func_t `f`
